## Natural history notes

A large thread-waisted wasp characterized by a black body, very narrow waist, yellow markings on the legs and body, and long dangling legs in flight. In Florida, the Yellow-legged Mud-dauber Wasp is found around buildings, bridges, sheds, porches, gardens, parks, forest edges, and other sheltered sites where females can build mud nests. Adults visit flowers for nectar, while females collect mud to build tubular nest cells and provision them with paralyzed spiders for the larvae; they are generally solitary and not aggressive unless handled.
